title: Prevention of Proliferation Financing and Other Matters Bill
what_it_is: Prevention of Proliferation Financing and Other Matters Bill

sections.label: Aligning sectors with FATF standards
sections.summary: The Bill aligns PSMD, moneylending, pawnbroking and legal services regimes with updated FATF standards on countering proliferation financing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This is in addition to existing FATF requirements on money laundering and terrorism financing risks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This Bill, therefore, seeks to clearly align the regulatory regimes for the PSMD, moneylending, pawnbroking and legal services sectors with the updated FATF standards on countering proliferation financing.

sections.label: Licence bar for financial crime convictions
sections.summary: The Bill prevents persons convicted of financial crime offences from obtaining licences or holding management functions in moneylending and pawnbroking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In particular, the Bill includes amendments to prevent persons convicted of offences relating to the prevention of financial crimes from obtaining relevant licences, or holding management functions in moneylending and pawnbroking businesses.

sections.label: Precious product value threshold
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends the definition of precious product to cover products priced above a prescribed value set at S$20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To close this gap, clause 4 of the Bill amends the definition of "precious product" to also cover any "precious product" priced above a prescribed value, which will be set at S$20,000, regardless of the value attributable to the PSPM.

sections.label: Asset-backed token and cash report offences
sections.summary: Clause 4 excludes digital payment tokens from the asset-backed token definition, and clause 12 creates an offence for incomplete or inaccurate cash transaction reports.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill also amends the existing definition of "asset-backed token" to exclude digital payment tokens from the PSPM Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This will avoid double regulation of PSMDs, as the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) already regulates digital payment token service providers under the Payment Services Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 12 of the Bill introduces a new offence in the PSPM Act for regulated dealers that submit incomplete or inaccurate cash transaction reports without reasonable excuse.

sections.label: Record-keeping after ceasing regulated dealer
sections.summary: The Bill requires regulated dealers to keep records for a prescribed period after ceasing to be a regulated dealer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: To prevent errant dealers from disposing of records to thwart investigations after they cease being regulated dealers, the Bill introduces a record-keeping requirement for regulated dealers to keep records, for a prescribed period after ceasing to be a regulated dealer.

sections.label: FATF proliferation financing risk requirements
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as an advocate and solicitor, arising from FATF October 2020 requirements to assess and mitigate proliferation financing risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I declare my interest as a practising advocate and solicitor in the Supreme Court of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This arises from new requirements introduced by the FATF in October 2020 for member states and reporting entities to assess the risk of proliferation financing in relation to their business and to take measures to mitigate the assessed risk.

sections.label: Seized assets in money laundering case
sections.summary: Assets seized in Singapore's biggest money laundering case rose to more than S$3 billion by January.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The assets seized in what is Singapore's biggest money laundering case have risen to more than S$3 billion by January.

sections.label: Lessons from money laundering case
sections.summary: A member asks what anti-money laundering compliance lessons the Government has learned from the case so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If banks, law firms, property companies or other businesses or professionals who assisted in property purchase or transfer of funds could have failed to detect or prevent transfer or use of money laundering proceeds, it can also happen to money lenders, dealers of precious stones and precious metals, not to mention, our neighbourhood pawnbrokers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am mindful that investigation is pending but I would like to ask the Government whether it is able to share what are, to date, the lessons which we have learned from the case so far as far as anti-money laundering (AML) compliance is concerned?

sections.label: Bill aligns laws with FATF standards
sections.summary: The Bill aligns Singapore's laws with FATF international standards to combat illicit financial flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The illicit funds of approximately $3 billion in seized or frozen assets, exposes the potential vulnerabilities within our financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It also underscores the critical need to fortify our defences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill aligns Singapore's laws with international standards set out by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), to effectively combat illicit financial flows and safeguard our reputation as a trusted financial hub.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill, confident it will safeguard Singapore's financial integrity and trusted financial hub position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The road ahead will not be easy, but we will walk it together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I stand in support of this Bill, confident it will safeguard Singapore's financial integrity, and solidify our position as a trusted financial hub.

sections.label: Compliance costs for impacted sectors
sections.summary: Impacted sectors will face significantly increased compliance costs, including a compliance officer role and new monitoring systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, we have to recognise that the impacted sectors will also face some major challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There will be a significant increase in compliance costs including the establishment of a compliance officer role as well as an increase in operational costs related to the development of specific training programmes and investment in new monitoring systems.

sections.label: Moneylenders and new regulations
sections.summary: A member asks how long businesses will be given to implement the new rules, noting risks to moneylenders and borrowers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the moneylending business, if a significant number of moneylenders face difficulties in renewing licenses due to these new regulations, there could be a reduction in available lending options in the market, limiting choices for borrowers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since many business owners, especially SMEs, may face challenges when adopting the proposed changes and regulations, how long will such businesses be given for implementation of these new rules?

sections.label: Inter-agency committee on financial crimes
sections.summary: An inter-agency Steering Committee leads whole-of-Government effort overseeing Singapore's national strategy for preventing financial crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The whole-of-Government effort is led by an inter-agency Steering Committee, which oversees the formulation and implementation of Singapore's national strategy for preventing financial crimes.

sections.label: FATF standards and presidency
sections.summary: Bill amendments align regulatory regimes with updated FATF standards on countering proliferation financing; Singapore nominated Mr T Raja Kumar, appointed FATF President in March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Bill before us today seek to align our regulatory regimes with the recent updates to the FATF standards in relation to countering proliferation financing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: More recently, Singapore nominated Mr T Raja Kumar from MHA to run for the position of FATF President.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: He was appointed by the FATF Plenary in March 2022 for a two-year term between 30 June 2022 and 1 July 2024.

sections.label: Anti-money laundering regime review
sections.summary: An Inter-Ministerial Committee chaired by Second Minister for Finance Ms Indranee Rajah reviews Singapore's anti-money laundering regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: An Inter-Ministerial Committee chaired by the Second Minister for Finance, Ms Indranee Rajah, has been formed to review Singapore's anti-money laundering regime and keep our regime up to date with increasingly sophisticated crimes.

sections.label: Digital payment token and casino regulation
sections.summary: Singapore required licensing and supervision for digital payment token services in 2020; 11 individuals were convicted for casino money laundering from 2010 to September 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2020, Singapore was one of the first jurisdictions in the world to tighten our regime by requiring licensing and supervision for providers of digital payment token services and imposing requirements to counter money laundering and terrorism financing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From 2010, when the two casinos opened, to September 2023, 11 individuals were detected using criminal proceeds in the casinos and were prosecuted and convicted for money laundering offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: GRA also conducts regular inspections of the casino operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It will also strengthen the regulatory regime for PSMDs and improve operational effectiveness in regulating PSMDs.
